title: Heterogeneous GPU Fleet Sampler - microbench notes
content:
Notes to self - high-level goal:
Run a quick sampling experiment across a mixed fleet to understand per-instance shape and cross-tenant variance when traffic is routed heterogeneously (A100 / H100 / L4). Focus: p50/p90/p99 behavior at short bursts and sustained QPS, plus warm vs cold KV-cache impact.

Environment / setup:
- Models: 13B distilled open-variant (baseline), same checkpoint compiled for cuda (float16) and for quantized path (4-bit int8-like).
- Hardware sampled: H100-80GB (hw-A), A100-40GB (hw-B), L4-48GB (hw-C) — all in same region.
- Pod config: 1-gpu per pod, 16 CPU cores reserved, 64GB RAM host.
- Runtime: continuous-batching enabled (batching window 15ms), KV cache enabled.
- Routing: round-robin assignment across fleet for initial run; later runs weight by 60/30/10 to simulate skewed capacity.
- Observability: token-level latencies, per-request trace id, GPU SM util, host CPU, PCIe bandwidth counters.

Test matrix:
- Sequences: short(64 tokens), medium(512), long(2048).
- Batch sizes: auto (runtime decides), fixed 1, fixed 4, fixed 8.
- Arrival patterns: poisson (mean lambda=25 qps), stair-step ramp (0->300 qps over 2m), sudden 1s spike to 1200 qps (burst).
- Warm states: cold (empty KV cache, cold model), warm (primed with 1000 requests, KV hit-rate ~75%).
- Duration: 10 runs of 5 minutes each per combination; pick representative ones here.

Quick test plan (practical):
1) Baseline single-hw runs (hw-A/hw-B/hw-C) with medium seq=512, auto batching, poisson 25 qps.
2) Interleaved heterogeneous run (round-robin) with same sequence and arrival.
3) Skewed weighting run to stress A100-primary with overflow to others.
4) Cold-start spike to 1200 qps for 10s to observe tail and preemption behavior.
5) Quantized path vs float16 path A/B compare.

Selected results (raw highlights) — aggregated across 5m windows, median of runs:
- Single-hw Baseline (seq=512, auto batch):
  - hw-A (H100): p50=18ms, p90=32ms, p99=110ms, throughput sustained=460 qps, mean GPU SM% 78%
  - hw-B (A100): p50=22ms, p90=40ms, p99=220ms, throughput sustained=410 qps, mean GPU SM% 72%
  - hw-C (L4): p50=45ms, p90=120ms, p99=650ms, throughput sustained=140 qps, mean GPU SM% 54%

- Heterogeneous round-robin (equal weights) + same seq:
  - observed effective p50=24ms, p90=60ms, p99=340ms. Notice super-linear p99 compared to weighted average — occasional long tails when a request hit L4 or when A100 pods respawned. Throughput ~380 qps.

- Skewed routing (60% H100 / 30% A100 / 10% L4):
  - overall p50=20ms, p90=35ms, p99=190ms. Better than round-robin because heavier traffic went to H100 but p99 still shows spikes when overflow land on L4.

- Cold spike (1s to 1200 qps, seq=64 short):
  - Observed 6–12s of elevated p99 (1–5s p99>1s), tail dominated by pods creating kernels and compiling CUDA kernels + lazy layers. KV-cache empty meant no prefix reuse. Instances that were recently spun down had the worst impact.
  - Autoscaler created new pods but provisioning lag (container start + model load) was the bigger contributor than GPU kernel warmup.

- Quantized path (4-bit-ish) vs float16 on hw-B:
  - Seq=512, quantized: p50=28ms, p90=60ms, p99=210ms, throughput=520 qps (better throughput), but higher variance p90/p99 due to extra CPU postprocessing step for dequantization and occasional cache thrash.

Observability notes / signals correlated with tails:
- Host CPU > 80% correlated with p99 spikes when multiple concurrent dequantize threads run (especially on A100).
- PCIe axial counters showed short bursts of 2–3x traffic during cache misses (reloading KV into GPU memory) and coincided with p99 jumps.
- Pod restarts during test (2/50) coincided with 1–2% of requests experiencing >2s latency (startup + model load). Need better warm pool / spinup strategy.
- Batching window =15ms is good for throughput but increases p50 a tiny bit; decreasing to 5ms reduces p50 ~6–8ms at cost of throughput ~8–10%.

Mini ASCII chart (p99 across fleet over 5m heterogeneous run):
Time -> |+++++----++++++-----++++++|
H100 p99 (ms):  [  80   120    95   110 ]
A100 p99 (ms):  [  150  210    180  230 ]
L4   p99 (ms):  [  500  650    700  620 ]
Interpretation: spikes align with L4 involvement and with host CPU climbs.

Quick conclusions / hypotheses:
- Heterogeneous fleets without routing awareness produce worse tails than expected (not just weighted average) — the slowest tier dominates tail latency when any fraction of traffic hits it.
- Warm pools (keep-alive, paused-but-warm) and KV-cache priming dramatically reduce short-burst tail; but they cost memory footprint. Tradeoff: maintain 10–20% warm headroom to avoid 1–2s tails on spikes.
- Quantization increases throughput but can add CPU-side variance; ensure worker CPU headroom if we push quantized paths.
- Autoscaler latency (container start + model load) is the critical path for spikes >500 qps; consider pre-warm or faster model mounting (shared memory snapshots?).

Action items / next runs:
- Run a focussed experiment: schedule flows that intentionally avoid L4 for p99-sensitive routes and measure end-to-end SLO compliance. (Ticket: INF-831)
- Test warm-pool size tradeoffs: 0%, 10%, 25% warm headroom, measure memory cost vs p99 reduction.
- Re-run quantized path with dedicated extra vCPUs (reserve 4 extra cores) to validate CPU contention hypothesis.
- Implement a lightweight health-weighted router: prefer H100/A100 for low-latency tags; bench again to quantify p99 improvement.
- Add synthetic kernel-compile profiling to traces to separate 'model load' vs 'first kernel compile' impact.

Random notes / TODOs:
- Add a transient flag to avoid routing any short-seq (<128 tokens) requests to L4 until warmed. Quick patch in router could help production tests.
- Talk to infra about faster model snapshot restore (was mentioned in meeting with Marco).

End of scratchpad. Keep this around until follow-ups complete.

-- Riley
